newsitem.title: USA: AMBI to buy nutrition company.
newsitem.headline: AMBI to buy nutrition company.

text.p: AMBI Inc said on Friday that it has agreed to buy privately-owned Nutrition 21 for $10 million in cash and 500,000 shares of AMBI common stock.
Based on today's current AMBI's share price of 2-1/2, the deal carries a value of about $11.25 million.

The parties expect to complete the deal within two months, AMBI said in a statement. As part of the deal, AMBI agreed to make contingent payments based on achieving certain sales levels in the next four years, and to pay royalties over future sales of new, patented products, it added.

San Diego-based Nutrition 21 develops and markets nutrition products and dietary supplements. For the 1996 year, it recorded pre-tax income of more than $6 million. Nutrition's founder and chief executive, Herbert Boynton, agreed to stay on as a consultant after the merger, AMBI said. The closing of
the transaction is subject to the execution of a binding agreement, approval by the board of directors of AMBI and the partners of Nutrition 21, and other terms and conditions, the company said.
"This acquisition will get us on the road to profitability," said Fredric Price, AMBI's chief executive. "Our goal would be to break even in our next fiscal year," ending June 30, 1998.
AMBI posted a loss of $0.17 per share for the nine months ended March 31, compared with a $0.14 loss the period before.

Price added Nutrition had a gross operating profit in the last year of 40 percent. The company's sales topped $15 million in the last 12 months showing a 20 percent year-on-year growth in the first quarter, he said.
"We're going to look at more product acquisitions in the nutrition area," Price said.
